correctness.rationale: Exact Laplacian eigenvalues and spectral projector coefficients yield four-mode formulas. Positive edge formulas and the Bernstein subordination identity prove all edge and alpha<=1 signs; the two rescaled derivatives have strictly monotone or strictly convex forms, proving exact root counts. At \(\alpha=2\) the first endpoint derivative is zero but its second is negative; for \(\alpha>2\) it starts positive while rigorous negative tests at log2 and 2 force exactly two zeros. Uniform compact convergence at two distinct time scales and bracketing simple limit roots prove all three large-exponent limits. Independent direct matrix exponentiation on the actual checker.py path passed 1574 tests; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The four-site path is the first ordinary path with four distinct Laplacian eigenvalues and hence a natural minimal setting for competing four-mode signs. Complete all-exponent classification shows an unusual and structurally significant transition at \(\alpha=2\): initially positive transfer becomes negative later and finally recovers. The two recovery scales differ exponentially in exponent; this sharp benchmark is not a numerical accident or a minor refinement of near-alpha-one perturbation.
